nodes.description: The root lesion is biallelic loss of FBXO7, which encodes F-box only protein 7, the substrate-recognition subunit of an SCF (SKP1-CUL1-F-box) E3 ubiquitin-ligase complex. nodes.description: A contested branch. FBXO7 was reported to be required for Parkin recruitment to depolarised mitochondria, mitofusin-1 ubiquitination and PINK1/Parkin-mediated mitophagy in FBXO7-knockdown cells; a later systematic study of clean FBXO7 knockouts in HeLa cells and iNeurons found no defect in Parkin recruitment, mitophagic flux or mitochondrial clearance, arguing against a general role. The node is therefore provisional and carries both the supporting and refuting evidence. It conforms to the mitochondrial-dysfunction module's mitophagy anchor.

evidence.reference_title: The Parkinson's disease-linked proteins Fbxo7 and Parkin interact to mediate mitophagy.
evidence.snippet: Cells with reduced Fbxo7 expression showed deficiencies in translocation of Parkin to mitochondria, ubiquitination of mitofusin 1 and mitophagy.

evidence.reference_title: PARK15/FBXO7 is dispensable for PINK1/Parkin mitophagy in iNeurons and HeLa cell systems.
evidence.snippet: We find that FBXO7-/- cells have no demonstrable defect in: (i) kinetics of pUb accumulation, (ii) pUb puncta on mitochondria by super-resolution imaging, (iii) recruitment of Parkin and autophagy machinery to damaged mitochondria, (iv) mitophagic flux, and (v) mitochondrial clearance as quantified by global proteomics.

nodes.description: FBXO7-SCF ubiquitinates the proteasome subunit PSMA2 and is required for proteasome assembly, so loss of FBXO7 reduces proteasome activity and ubiquitin-dependent protein degradation - the branch best supported in vivo, where FBXO7-knockout mice show reduced proteasome activity. This node conforms to the loss-of-proteostasis module's proteostasis-network-decline anchor.

nodes.description: Degeneration of substantia nigra pars compacta dopaminergic neurons, the shared downstream convergence point of the monogenic parkinsonisms. A dopamine-neuron-specific Fbxo7 knockout produces a slow, progressive loss of midbrain dopamine neurons, driven mechanistically by increased RPL23 (a ribosomal-stress sensor) that inhibits MDM2 and so activates a pro-apoptotic p53 programme. The node conforms to the module's nigrostriatal-degeneration anchor; the neuron-apoptotic-process term follows that anchor.
